Sungmin · Listen & Shadow 11

Why Grad School, In English — the three whys and the numbers
D O   E N G L I S H   W I T H   B R I A N
PART 1 · CATCHING UP
👤 Interviewer
How's the arm doing?
팔은 좀 어때요?
arm — 팔
💬 Sungmin
It's still healing. I'm staying off the court for now.
아직 낫는 중이에요. 당분간 테니스는 쉬고 있어요.
heal — 낫다 · stay off ~ — ~를 당분간 안 하다
같은 패턴으로 — It's still sore. I'm staying off the gym for now. · She's still recovering, so she's staying off her bike.
💬 Sungmin
Things at school are still ongoing.
학교 일은 계속 돌아가고 있고요.
ongoing — 계속 진행 중인
같은 패턴으로 — The project is still ongoing. · The renovation is ongoing until spring.
PART 2 · WHY TRANSITION EDUCATION
👤 Interviewer
Why transition education — why that, out of everything?
왜 전환교육인가요?
transition — 전환, 옮겨가는 시기
💬 Sungmin
The short answer is that the hardest part starts after they leave school.
짧게 답하면, 학생들이 학교를 떠난 다음이 제일 위태로워요.
the short answer is ~ — 짧게 답하면 ~
같은 패턴으로 — The short answer is that nobody prepares them for it. · The short answer is money.
💬 Sungmin
What I kept seeing was parents asking what comes next — and no one had an answer.
제가 계속 목격한 건, 학부모님들이 졸업 다음을 물어보는데 답할 게 없다는 거였어요.
what I kept seeing was ~ — 제가 계속 목격한 건 ~ · what comes next — 그다음에 오는 것
같은 패턴으로 — What I kept seeing was students repeating the same mistake. · What I kept seeing was teachers working alone.
💬 Sungmin
It comes down to preparing them for the life that comes after school.
결국 학교가 끝난 뒤의 삶을 준비시키는 문제예요.
it comes down to ~ — 결국 ~의 문제다
같은 패턴으로 — It comes down to time. · It comes down to how early we start.
PART 3 · WHY POLICY MATTERS
👤 Interviewer
Why do national policies matter inside your classroom?
국가 정책이 교실 안에서 왜 중요한가요?
policy — 정책
💬 Sungmin
A policy ends up as my timetable.
정책은 결국 제 시간표가 돼요.
end up as ~ — 결국 ~가 되다 · timetable — 시간표
같은 패턴으로 — A good idea ends up as extra work. · The plan ended up as a one-page form.
💬 Sungmin
For the free-semester program, I built a course around our own neighborhood.
자유학기제 때 저는 우리 지역을 주제로 수업을 하나 만들었어요.
build a course — 수업을 만들다 · neighborhood — 동네, 지역
같은 패턴으로 — I built a lesson around their part-time jobs. · She built a class around local shops.
💬 Sungmin
The closer it is to daily life, the better they follow it.
일상과 가까울수록 학생들이 훨씬 잘 따라와요.
the closer ~, the better ~ — ~할수록 더 ~하다
같은 패턴으로 — The shorter the task, the better they focus. · The simpler the words, the better they remember.
PART 4 · WHY BASIC SKILLS
👤 Interviewer
Why start with reading, writing, and counting?
왜 읽기·쓰기·셈하기부터인가요?
counting — 셈하기
💬 Sungmin
Taking a bus, paying for something, talking to people — it all starts there.
버스를 타고, 값을 치르고, 사람과 얘기하는 일이 전부 거기서 시작하니까요.
it all starts there — 모든 게 거기서 시작된다
같은 패턴으로 — Cooking, cleaning, budgeting — it all starts at home. · Reading, asking, checking — it all starts with confidence.
💬 Sungmin
Most of the students I met had already given up after failing again and again.
제가 만난 학생들 대부분은 반복된 실패로 이미 지쳐 있었어요.
give up — 포기하다 · again and again — 반복해서
같은 패턴으로 — Most of them had already stopped trying. · He had already given up before the first class.
💬 Sungmin
So I think it has to be rebuilt into skills they can actually use.
그래서 저는 교과 지식보다 실제로 쓸 수 있는 기술로 바꿔야 한다고 봐요.
rebuild into ~ — ~로 다시 만들다
같은 패턴으로 — It has to be rebuilt into something simpler. · The manual was rebuilt into a one-page guide.
PART 5 · THE NUMBERS
👤 Interviewer
Can you put that in numbers?
숫자로 말해볼까요?
put ~ in numbers — 숫자로 말하다
💬 Sungmin
According to a national survey, only about three in ten graduates find a job.
국가 조사에 따르면, 졸업생 열 명 중 세 명 정도만 일자리를 찾아요.
according to ~ — ~에 따르면 · survey — 조사
같은 패턴으로 — According to the report, only one in five applied. · According to our data, most families stay nearby.
💬 Sungmin
Most of the rest stay home.
나머지 대부분은 집에 머물러요.
the rest — 나머지
같은 패턴으로 — Most of the rest dropped out. · The rest stayed for another year.
💬 Sungmin
Those who do work stay about five years, then wait more than a decade for the next job.
일을 시작한 학생들도 대략 5년쯤 다니고, 그다음엔 10년 넘게 다음 일을 못 찾아요.
decade — 10년
같은 패턴으로 — Those who do apply wait months for an answer. · He waited more than a decade to go back.
💬 Sungmin
That number is why I'm going back to study.
그 숫자 때문에 제가 대학원에 가려는 거예요.
go back to study — 다시 공부하러 가다
같은 패턴으로 — That number is why I changed my lesson plan. · That's why I started this project.
💬 Sungmin
I want to change the odds my students are facing.
제 학생들이 마주할 확률을 바꾸고 싶어요.
odds — 확률, 가능성 · face — 마주하다
같은 패턴으로 — I want to change the odds for the next class. · The odds are against them right now.
PART 6 · DON'T SAY IT TWICE
👤 Interviewer
Say that again — but without the same word.
방금 그 말, 다른 말로 해볼까요?
without ~ — ~ 없이
💬 Sungmin
My students — the kids I teach, the ones leaving school soon.
학생들 — 제가 가르치는 아이들, 곧 학교를 떠날 친구들.
the ones ~ — ~하는 사람들
같은 패턴으로 — My learners · the young people I work with
💬 Sungmin
Transition — the move into adult life, what comes next as their reality.
전환 — 어른의 삶으로 넘어가는 시기, 졸업 다음에 오는 현실.
the move into ~ — ~로 넘어가는 것 · reality — 현실
같은 패턴으로 — life after graduation · what waits for them outside
💬 Sungmin
Support — back them up, walk them through it, help them step by step.
지원한다 — 곁에서 도와주고, 하나하나 같이 해보는 것.
back someone up — 뒤에서 받쳐주다 · walk someone through ~ — 하나하나 같이 해보다
같은 패턴으로 — help them along · stay with them until they can do it
💬 Sungmin
Important — it's the key point, and it's what we should focus on.
중요하다 — 이게 핵심이고, 여기에 초점을 맞춰야 해요.
key point — 핵심 · focus on ~ — ~에 집중하다
같은 패턴으로 — it makes the difference · it's at the heart of this
💬 Sungmin
Difficult — it's not easy, and they hit a wall.
어렵다 — 쉽지 않고, 벽에 부딪히는 거죠.
hit a wall — 벽에 부딪히다, 더 못 나아가다
같은 패턴으로 — it's a struggle · it doesn't come easily
